question: How does the guṇa-transcendent one remain steady without aiming at fruit?
premises: equal honor and dishonor marks the guṇa-transcendent one
right knowing keeps him from falling from own form
steady intellect does not aim at fruit
inference: The guṇa-transcendent agent acts through body and senses while remaining unmoved by results.
uncertainties: fused sandhi forms are glossed as wholes
verse number token retained as paratext-like numeral
plain_english: He who is equal in honor and dishonor, friend and foe, abandoning fruits of all undertakings, is called beyond the strands; though appearing ignorant, he stands without discrimination, and from right knowing he does not fall from his own form.
